expected.note: Cookie store HMAC key comes from config, but config.json key is misspelled 'sessionkey:' so Sessionkey is empty (and the intended key G0Vw444 is hardcoded in the repo); anyone can sign a govwa cookie with govwa_session=true,id=N to log in as any user (verified with securecookie v1.1.1).
UnsafeQueryGetData builds SQL with fmt.Sprintf from uid; reached at level low from /sqli1 (Uid cookie) and /sqli2 (uid query param), allowing UNION/error-based SQLi.
/sqli1 uses the client-set Uid cookie instead of the session id to load a profile, so changing the cookie reveals any user's name/city/phone (also at level high).
/sqli2 loads the profile for the uid query param with no ownership check; any logged-in user reads other users' PII at both levels.
/xss2 loads the profile for the uid query param with no ownership check; any logged-in user reads other users' PII.
At level low the term param is wrapped in template.HTML after only a bypassable script-tag regex, e.g. /xss1?term= gives reflected XSS.
uid param is formatted unquoted into an inline script and marked template.HTML; HTMLEscapeString (level high) does not neutralize JS context, so uid=1;alert(document.cookie) executes at both levels.
At level low the update target uid is only compared to the client-controlled Uid cookie; setting both to a victim id overwrites any user's profile.
Integrity signature is an unkeyed MD5 of uid, so an attacker computes md5(victim_id) and updates any user's profile at level low.

OTP is a single hardcoded unsalted MD5 (of 256612) shared by all users with no rate limit, and the verdict is only enforced client-side; trivially cracked, brute-forced or bypassed by tampering the response.
Passwords are stored and compared as unsalted MD5 (user.go:88, seeded in setup/function.go:19), so leaked hashes (e.g. via the SQLi) are instantly cracked.
/setup and /setupaction have no AuthCheck; an unauthenticated POST act=cr drops and recreates the Users and Profile tables, wiping data and resetting accounts to default passwords.
Setup seeds fixed accounts admin/govwaadmin and user1/govwauser1 (documented in README and user.go comments), which anyone can log in with or restore via the unauthenticated reset.

Connect() opens two new sql.DB pools per call and never closes them, and it runs on almost every request including unauthenticated GET /login; repeated requests leak MySQL connections until max_connections is hit (DoS).

must_not_report.reason: SafeQueryGetData uses a constant query with a ? placeholder via Prepare/QueryRow; uid is bound, so there is no SQLi.
Constant SQL with a bound ? parameter; no injection.
UPDATE uses a constant statement with bound parameters; no injection (the authz issue is in the callers).
Login query is a constant prepared statement with bound username and hash; not injectable.
The string-concatenated CREATE DATABASE uses Dbname from the server-side config file, which no request can influence.
template.HTML wraps a fixed string plus a MySQL/driver error message; no request data reaches it, so there is no XSS.
template.HTML of a link built from config.Fullurl (server config), not user input.
template.HTML is used only with constant message strings.
UnSafeRender is never called and uses html/template (auto-escaping) anyway; the name is misleading.
ServeFiles with http.Dir cleans the path and blocks ../ traversal outside public/.

debatable.note: ACAO * with Allow-Credentials true on JSON responses; browsers refuse credentialed reads with a wildcard origin, so it is a misconfiguration and not exploitable.
State-changing POSTs (/idor1action, /idor2action, /setlevel) have no CSRF token and the session cookie has no SameSite; exploitability depends on browser Lax defaults.
Security mode (low/high) is read from a client-set Level cookie, so any user can downgrade the protections; this is the lab's difficulty switch by design.
Uid/Level cookies are set without HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite.
Raw SQL error text is rendered to the user at level low (CWE-209), which helps error-based SQLi; the root cause is the SQLi.
CapturePanic returns the internal panic or error message to the client.
GetCookie dereferences a nil cookie when the cookie is missing, which panics; the panic is recovered (CapturePanic/net/http), so the result is a 500 and not a crash.
User-Agent regex denylist for sqlmap is trivially bypassed; it is not a real control, but the vulnerability is the SQLi itself.
User-Agent is logged unsanitized (CWE-117 log forging).
Settings page shows MySQL version and OS to any logged-in user.
DB credentials are committed in config.json (despite .gitignore), and docker-compose.yml:21-25 has the MySQL root password and exposes port 3307; these are local lab settings.
Stateless cookie store: logout only expires the browser cookie, and a stolen cookie stays valid server-side (securecookie maxAge 30 days).
Session id is formatted into an inline script via template.HTML; the value is a server-set integer and could only be changed by forging one's own session (self-XSS).
Login has no lockout or rate limiting, so it is open to online brute force.
Final image has no USER directive, so it runs as root.
Session cookie is set with HttpOnly false on purpose (and no Secure), so the XSS bugs can steal the govwa session cookie. [review: sink outside scanned files, or intentional lab setting]
